title: Animals and their babies
keyIdea: Animals have babies. A baby is a small one of the same kind of animal, and it grows into a grown-up like its mummy. Many babies have their own names: a lamb is a baby sheep, a calf is a baby cow, a kitten is a baby cat and a duckling is a baby duck.

kid: Animals have babies. A baby is small. Its mummy is big.
A lamb is a baby sheep. A calf is a baby cow. A kitten is a baby cat. A duckling is a baby duck.
A puppy is a baby dog. A chick is a baby chicken. A piglet is a baby pig. A foal is a baby horse.
Babies grow and grow. A kitten grows into a cat. It does not turn into a dog!
adult: This topic is about matching common farm and pet animals with their young, learning the special names for the babies, and knowing that a baby grows up into the same kind of animal as its parent. It builds the early idea of life cycles and offspring that later science work depends on.

In the lab your child walks four babies to their mothers, names the baby of a dog, sheep, pig and horse, taps to grow a kitten into a cat and a chick into a hen, sorts six animals into babies and grown-ups, and finds a lamb, chick and calf and then their mothers on a farm page.

Common mistakes: using one baby word for every animal (calling a lamb a puppy); mixing up the chick and the duckling, which both hatch as small fluffy birds; thinking a baby stays small, or grows into a different animal; and judging only by size, so a big lamb next to a small breed of sheep can confuse. Say both words together: a lamb is a baby sheep.
Picture books, farm visits and toy animals all help. Hold up a toy sheep and ask, "Where is her baby? What is it called?" Then swap roles and let your child ask you.

familyTip: Next time you read a farm book or see animals out and about, play 'find the baby': spot a young animal, say its name, then find its mummy. Start with lamb and sheep or calf and cow, and add one new name each week.

practice.hint: A lamb is a baby. Which big animal is woolly like it?
practice.explain: A lamb is a baby sheep, so its mummy is a sheep.

practice.prompt: A cat has {n} babies. What are they called?
practice.hint: Think of the name for a baby cat.
practice.explain: Baby cats are kittens, so the cat has {n} kittens. Puppies are baby dogs.

practice.prompt: A calf grows and grows. What will it be?
practice.hint: A calf is a baby. Who is its mummy?
practice.explain: A calf is a baby cow, so it grows into a cow. Babies do not stay small.

practice.prompt: A hen sits on {n} eggs. What comes out?
practice.hint: What is a baby chicken called?
practice.explain: Baby chickens are chicks, so {n} chicks hatch. Ducklings come from duck eggs.

pool.hint: A calf is a baby. It drinks milk from a big farm animal.
pool.explain: A calf is a baby cow. Its mummy is a cow.

pool.prompt: {n} puppies are playing. What will they grow into?
pool.hint: A puppy is a baby. Which grown-up is it a baby of?
pool.explain: Puppies are baby dogs, so all {n} puppies grow into dogs.

pool.prompt: A sheep and her lamb. Which one is the baby?
pool.hint: Babies are small. Grown-ups are big.
pool.explain: The small lamb is the baby. The big sheep is its mummy.

pool.prompt: A duckling grows up. What is it now?
pool.hint: A duckling is a baby. Who is its mummy?
pool.explain: A duckling is a baby duck, so it grows up into a duck, not a hen.

pool.prompt: What is a baby horse called?
pool.hint: It is the one we saw with the horse in the lab.
pool.explain: A baby horse is a foal. A piglet is a baby pig and a chick is a baby chicken.

pool.prompt: There are {n} piglets in the mud. Who is their mummy?
pool.explain: Piglets are baby pigs, so the mummy of all {n} piglets is a pig.

pool.prompt: What is a baby cat called?
pool.hint: It has its own name, not cat.
pool.explain: A baby cat is a kitten. A puppy is a baby dog.

pool.prompt: A chick hatches from an egg. Who is its mummy?
pool.hint: A chick is a baby. Which bird says cluck?
pool.explain: A chick is a baby chicken, and its mummy is a hen. A duck's baby is a duckling.

visual.caption: Whose baby is it? Find its mummy. Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: take babies home to their mummies, name the babies, grow a kitten and a chick, sort big and small, and find babies on a farm page.
